suppress.notes: False positive. CVE-2025-7962 is an SMTP injection vulnerability in org.eclipse.angus:angus-mail (Jakarta Mail), not angus-activation. angus-activation only handles MIME type resolution/DataHandler — it has no SMTP or mail-sending code path, so this CVE cannot apply to it. Confirmed as a known false positive against the dependency-check project itself (issues #8144 and #8211 on dependency-check/DependencyCheck). Pulled in transitively via jaxws-rt (JAX-WS Metro). Review date: 2027-01-08 (re-check if a new angus-activation CVE is filed, or if jaxws-rt drops the dependency).

False positive. CVE-2026-2586 and CVE-2026-2587 are RCE vulnerabilities in the GlassFish Administration Console (authenticated OS command execution) and the GlassFish gadget handler's server-side template rendering (unescaped EL expressions in XML). Both require a running GlassFish application server with its admin console — this project has neither; it runs on Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat. jaxb-impl here is only the JAXB runtime used by the JAX-WS Metro SOAP client (QSolutionsSoapAdapter), not an application server. The CPE match (cpe:2.3:a:eclipse:glassfish) is a known confusion between the jaxb-impl library artifact and the GlassFish product that used to bundle it. Pulled in transitively via jaxws-rt. Review date: 2027-01-08.

False positive / already remediated. CVE-2026-42582 affects netty-codec-http3 (HTTP/3 codec module) — this project does not use HTTP/3 anywhere; Netty is pulled in transitively via Lettuce (spring-boot-starter-data-redis), which only uses plain TCP. The generic "netty:netty" CPE (cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:4.1.135) does not distinguish between Netty modules, so it attaches to whichever io.netty:* jar the analyzer happens to process — observed on netty-transport in one run and netty-transport-native-unix-common in another, neither of which contains the affected HTTP/3 codec. This suppression is scoped to the whole io.netty group (not one artifact) so it survives that non-determinism. Additionally, the CVE was fixed upstream in Netty 4.1.133.Final — we are already on 4.1.135.Final (later than the fix), so even if the affected module were present it would not be vulnerable at this version. Review date: 2027-01-08.

False positive. CVE-2026-34477/34478/34479/34480/34481 and CVE-2025-68161 are all in log4j-core Layout implementation classes (Rfc5424Layout, XmlLayout, Log4j1XmlLayout, JsonTemplateLayout) — none of which exist in log4j-api, which only contains the logging facade (Logger, LogManager, Level, Marker). Confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=org.apache.logging.log4j` (2026-07-08): log4j-api is pulled in transitively as spring-boot-starter-logging -> log4j-to-slf4j -> log4j-api, a bridge that redirects Log4j2 API calls into SLF4J/Logback (our actual logging implementation). log4j-core is absent from the dependency tree entirely, so the vulnerable Layout classes cannot be on the classpath regardless of the log4j-api version. The generic "apache:log4j" CPE does not distinguish api from core. Review date: 2027-01-08 (re-check if any dependency ever pulls in log4j-core directly).
